parole.significato: A beetle, Prionoplus reticularis, endemic to New Zealand.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori huhu (“larval form of this beetle”), from Proto-Polynesian *fufu (“weevil”).

parole.significato: A longhorn beetle, Prionoplus reticularis, of the Cerambycidae family; the largest endemic beetle found in New Zealand.
parole.testo: From Māori huhu, which specifically refers to the larval form, from Proto-Polynesian *fufu.
Borrowed from Māori kahika, from Proto-Polynesian *kafika (“Malay apple”), from Proto-Oceanic *kapika.
Borrowed from Māori kāinga. Doublet of ʻāina.

parole.significato: A conifer of the genus Agathis, found in Australasia and Melanesia, especially Agathis australis.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori kauri from Proto-Polynesian *kauquli, from *kau (“tree”) + *quli (“black”), originally referring to Samoan ebony ("Diospyros samoensis").

parole.significato: Power, prestige; specifically, a form of supernatural energy in Polynesian religion that inheres in things or people.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori mana, ultimately from Proto-Polynesian *mana, from Proto-Oceanic *mana. The use of "mana" for "magical energy" in role-playing games originated from Larry Niven, when he wrote the short story, "Not Long Before the End", in 1969. parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori moa, from Proto-Polynesian *moa (“fowl”).

parole.significato: A Maori dirge, or song for the dead.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori tangi (“lament, mourning, funeral ceremony”).

parole.significato: Podocarpus totara, a podocarp tree endemic to New Zealand.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Māori tōtara, from Proto-Polynesian *tara (“barb, prong”), from Proto-Oceanic *tala, referring to its mature leaves which resemble spines of the spot-fin porcupinefish (Diodon hystrix).
Borrowed from Māori wahine (“woman”), from Proto-Polynesian *fafine.
